name: Fallingwater
kicker: Frank Lloyd Wright’s house · Built directly over a Pennsylvania waterfall
briefing: Frank Lloyd Wright convinced department-store owner Edgar Kaufmann to build his family’s weekend home directly over a waterfall on Bear Run in rural Pennsylvania, not just near it. Wright cantilevered concrete terraces out above the falls so the sound of rushing water fills the house, a style he called organic architecture. Kaufmann later joked that the leaky, sagging house should be nicknamed “Rising Mildew.”

tossups.p: Structural engineers Mendel Glickman and William Peters, who also worked on the dendriform columns of Wright’s Johnson Wax headquarters, helped this building’s reinforced-concrete terraces cantilever out over a creek using a T-shaped plan anchored to a hillside. A Hollywood art director modeled the fictional Vandamm Residence in _North by Northwest_ on this real building.
tossups.r: Builders quietly added extra steel bars to its terraces, against the wishes of its architect, after doubting that his daring cantilever design would hold. For 10 points, name this Pennsylvania house built over a waterfall for the Kaufmann family by Frank Lloyd Wright.

tossups.p: A sculpture by Jacques Lipchitz called _Mother and Child_ is displayed at this building, whose kitchen was once run by a cook named Elsie Henderson. Its steel window frames were painted in a reddish-orange shade that its architect nicknamed “Cherokee red.”
tossups.r: Leaks and mold earned this building a nickname joking about its constant dampness. For 10 points, name this Pennsylvania weekend home built over Bear Run for the Kaufmann family by Frank Lloyd Wright.

tossups.p: Its owner, a Pittsburgh department-store magnate, originally expected his family’s weekend home to simply offer a view of a nearby waterfall. Instead, the architect cantilevered the house directly above the falls, reportedly to that owner’s own early displeasure, so that the sound of rushing water would fill its rooms.
tossups.r: Frank Lloyd Wright designed this house for Edgar Kaufmann on a creek called Bear Run. For 10 points, name this organic-architecture landmark in rural Pennsylvania, famous for sitting directly above a waterfall.

tossups.p: Locally quarried Pottsville sandstone forms the vertical piers of this building, while all of its woodwork is black walnut from North Carolina. Its low parapets, only 26 inches tall, would not meet modern building codes.
tossups.r: Reinforced-concrete terraces, trimmed in “Cherokee red” steel, cantilever out above a Pennsylvania creek. For 10 points, name this Frank Lloyd Wright house built for the Kaufmann family over Bear Run.

tossups.p: By the late 1980s, the ends of this building’s terraces had sagged about seven inches. A restoration in the early 2000s threaded high-strength steel cables through its terraces to stop further sagging, part of a project costing over eleven million dollars.
tossups.r: Visitors today can tour this house, which the Western Pennsylvania Conservancy has owned since 1963. For 10 points, name this Pennsylvania home built directly above a waterfall by Frank Lloyd Wright.

tossups.p: In 2019, UNESCO named this building a World Heritage Site as one of eight buildings honored together under the title “The 20th-Century Architecture of Frank Lloyd Wright.” It had already been declared a U.S. National Historic Landmark back in 1976.
tossups.r: Its architect reportedly told its owner, “I want you to live with the waterfall, not to look at it.” For 10 points, name this Pennsylvania house cantilevered above Bear Run for the Kaufmann family.

tossups.p: This building is often called the finest example of “organic architecture,” Frank Lloyd Wright’s philosophy of designing structures that grow naturally out of their surroundings rather than sitting apart from them. Its design lets the roar of rushing water carry into nearly every room.
tossups.r: Reinforced-concrete terraces reach out from a central stone chimney to hang above a Pennsylvania creek. For 10 points, name this landmark, a weekend home Wright built for the Kaufmann family over Bear Run.

tossups.p: This building sits near the small town of Mill Run in Fayette County, Pennsylvania, about seventy miles southeast of Pittsburgh. Guests who stayed there over the decades included Albert Einstein and the painter Diego Rivera.
tossups.r: Frank Lloyd Wright cantilevered its concrete terraces directly above a waterfall on Bear Run. For 10 points, name this famous Pennsylvania house built for the Kaufmann family.

tossups.p: A massive stone chimney anchors the center of this building, from which cantilevered terraces stretch out in several directions above the creek below. Design work began in 1934, and the main house was finished by 1937.
tossups.r: This weekend retreat was built for department-store owner Edgar Kaufmann on a Pennsylvania creek called Bear Run. For 10 points, name this Frank Lloyd Wright masterpiece, a house built directly above its own waterfall.

tossups.p: Edgar Kaufmann jokingly nicknamed this house “Rising Mildew” after years of leaks and mold made it hard to keep dry. Despite those problems, it remains one of the most photographed houses in the world.
tossups.r: Frank Lloyd Wright designed it to hang directly above a waterfall on Bear Run. For 10 points, name this Pennsylvania house built for the Kaufmann family.

tossups.p: This house’s concrete terraces reach out over a waterfall instead of simply sitting beside it, letting its owners hear rushing water from inside nearly every room. Frank Lloyd Wright designed it in the style he called organic architecture.
tossups.r: It was built for the Kaufmann family of Pittsburgh on a creek called Bear Run. For 10 points, name this Pennsylvania house, considered Wright’s most famous residential design.

tossups.p: Albert Einstein and the painter Diego Rivera both visited this Pennsylvania house during the Kaufmann family’s ownership. Its terraces cantilever directly out over a waterfall on Bear Run, a design so bold that builders secretly reinforced it with extra steel.
tossups.r: Frank Lloyd Wright designed this house so its owners could live with, rather than merely look at, the waterfall beneath it. For 10 points, name this famous house in rural Pennsylvania.

tossups.p: This house in rural Pennsylvania was built directly on top of a waterfall rather than merely facing it. Its architect, Frank Lloyd Wright, called this style of blending buildings into nature “organic architecture.” Reinforced-concrete terraces stretch out from the house in several directions, seemingly floating above the rushing creek below.
tossups.r: It was designed as a weekend retreat for the Kaufmann family. For 10 points, name this famous Pennsylvania house built over Bear Run.

tossups.p: Frank Lloyd Wright designed this Pennsylvania house so a waterfall runs directly beneath it instead of merely past it. Builders used reinforced concrete to cantilever its terraces out over the creek below, and locally quarried stone forms its walls and central chimney.
tossups.r: Built for the Kaufmann family on a creek called Bear Run, this house is considered one of the finest examples of organic architecture. For 10 points, name this house, often called Wright’s masterpiece.

tossups.p: Frank Lloyd Wright designed this house for the Kaufmann family, cantilevering its concrete terraces directly over a waterfall on Bear Run in rural Pennsylvania. Its constant leaking and mold later earned it the joking nickname “Rising Mildew.”
tossups.r: Considered Wright’s masterpiece, this house is now a museum open to the public. For 10 points, name this Pennsylvania home built over its own waterfall.

trap.title: Which Frank Lloyd Wright building?
trap.body: Frank Lloyd Wright designed hundreds of buildings, and quiz bowl loves clueing several of them: the spiral Guggenheim Museum in New York, the lily-pad columns of the Johnson Wax Headquarters, and Wright’s own home and studio, Taliesin. A clue that just names Wright, “organic architecture,” or a cantilever could be pointing at any of these before it gets specific.
trap.fix: Listen for the waterfall. Bear Run, the Kaufmann family, Mill Run Pennsylvania, or “Rising Mildew” all mean Fallingwater. Lily-pad columns mean Johnson Wax. A spiral ramp in New York means the Guggenheim.
